source.paraphrase: Function size exceeds the selected limit.

invariants.why: Function size exceeds the selected limit.
invariants.fixHint: Extract a cohesive operation and preserve behavior with relevant tests.
invariants.avoid: Do not compress statements onto one line or split a single state machine into arbitrary fragments.

source.paraphrase: Function parameter count exceeds the selected limit.

invariants.why: Function parameter count exceeds the selected limit.
invariants.fixHint: Review whether the inputs describe a cohesive domain object.
invariants.avoid: Do not hide unrelated inputs in a generic options map; Python self/cls and variadic parameters count, Go receivers do not.

source.paraphrase: Control-flow nesting exceeds the selected limit.

invariants.why: Control-flow nesting exceeds the selected limit.
invariants.fixHint: Use an early return or name a cohesive inner operation.
invariants.avoid: Do not hide nesting in loops, switch/match branches or exception handlers.

source.paraphrase: A dot import obscures the package owning an identifier.

invariants.why: A dot import obscures the package owning an identifier.
invariants.fixHint: Use a named package qualifier, unless a reviewed DSL intentionally requires a dot import.
invariants.avoid: Do not replace a dot import with copied package identifiers.

source.work: Go standard library documentation, package io/ioutil
source.paraphrase: io/ioutil is deprecated. The same functionality is provided by package io or package os, and those should be preferred in new code.

invariants.why: New code that imports io/ioutil depends on a deprecated package whose functions are now thin wrappers around io and os.
invariants.fixHint: Call the replacement named in each function's doc: os.ReadFile, os.WriteFile, os.ReadDir, os.MkdirTemp, os.CreateTemp, io.ReadAll or io.Discard.
invariants.avoid: Do not rename the import or switch to a raw string path; the package is still io/ioutil.

source.work: Go standard library documentation, package context
source.paraphrase: Do not store Contexts inside a struct type; pass a Context explicitly to each function that needs it. Backward compatibility of an existing API is the exception the Go blog describes.

invariants.why: A context stored in a struct outlives the call it belongs to, so callers cannot set a deadline or cancel one operation without affecting every method on the value.
invariants.fixHint: Remove the field and add ctx context.Context as the first parameter of each method that needs it.
invariants.avoid: Do not embed the context, store a pointer to it or hide it in a nested struct. Keep a context field only to preserve an existing public API, under a reviewed exclusion.

source.work: Go standard library documentation, package context
source.paraphrase: The Context should be the first parameter, typically named ctx.

invariants.why: A context in any other position breaks the convention callers and tools rely on to find and propagate cancellation.
invariants.fixHint: Move ctx context.Context to the first parameter and update the callers. Test helpers may keep *testing.T or testing.TB before it.
invariants.avoid: Do not move the context into an options struct or a struct field to satisfy the order.

source.paraphrase: An empty select{} blocks the calling goroutine forever.

invariants.why: select {} permanently halts the goroutine, leaking goroutine stacks and preventing graceful termination.
invariants.fixHint: Use context cancellation (<-ctx.Done()) or signal coordination instead of an empty select.
invariants.avoid: Do not use select {} to sleep or wait forever.
